summary: Yasuo Deguchi is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology and held multiple posts at Kyoto University, including professor and dean, later joining ZEN University and founding the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.
Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1991) and as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as a technical official at the Nara National Museum from around 1994 to 2002 and took up a post at Kyoto University around 2002.

Yasuo Matsunami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995-2006) and was an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group until 2010.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyo Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.

Yasuo Yuasa was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held academic posts at Osaka, Otemae, and Ryukoku universities, and was a professor and professor emeritus at Nagoya University.

Yasusaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1892 to 1896. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1897-1906) and Kyushu University (~1906-1928).

Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and the University of Leipzig (attested 2015), and a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1986-2004) and Koyasan University (~2004), and served as president of Mikkyo Kenkyukai (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yeshe Thubten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera Monastery and under teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977-1978) and founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT.
Yeshi Dhonden was a Tibetology scholar who studied at Chakpori Medical College under Khyenrab Norbu. He founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961 and served as its director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner.

Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She served as dean and department head at University of the West and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who is attested in 2026 as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock. He became an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2011.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied at Fu Jen Catholic, Yenching, and Harvard universities, learning under Yinke Chen. He served as a professor at Peking University from around 1952 to 1998.

Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at Harvard. He held professorships and posts at Harvard, Yale, Princeton, the University of Michigan, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Yingguang Qu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Puren Bai, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche.
